writeup: TIC 320341748 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 16.254118 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 4.02% dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 12.6, though the centroid offset of 6.3 arcsec warrants attention. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. One open question remains: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, which may indicate the true orbital period is actually twice the initial automated detection suggested - a pattern the corrected period accounts for but which should be noted as an outstanding feature of this candidate system.
